title: Crown of the Grave: a playable browser roguelite built by directing an AI coding agent
author: DuckQuack8
selftext:
I’m No-Bullets, the creator directing Crown of the Grave. It’s a free, in-development dark fantasy roguelite for PC browsers, with a Windows download and optional donations. The current public alpha is 0.9.2: [https://no-bullets.itch.io/crown-of-the-grave](https://no-bullets.itch.io/crown-of-the-grave)



The design I’m working toward is character-specific builds with choices that matter beyond a stat increase. You start as the Knight and can unlock the Gravecaller and Ashen Hunter. In the Foundry, rescuing prisoners gives a soul memory that changes with your weapon and affects the region’s final encounter. Movement and dodging are manual; attacks aim automatically. Keyboard is recommended.



AI disclosure: AI is used extensively throughout development, including code, visuals, writing and procedural audio, and helped draft this post. I direct the design and iteration; I’m not claiming to have hand-coded the game. There is no live generative AI running while you play.



The workflow has been to turn a design request into a local build, exercise it across character/weapon combinations, then test saves, the browser and Windows before shipping. For example, the latest patch fixed Continue losing the last movement direction. Scripted long-run tests help catch regressions, but they cannot tell me whether a real person finds the opening readable or a build enjoyable. That’s the gap I’m trying to close.



If you try it, I’d particularly value the first moment you felt lost, an upgrade that was difficult to understand, or a weapon/build that felt awkward. Your character, weapon and seed help reproduce a problem. There’s a feedback board on the game page. I’m also interested in how other AI-assisted developers check game feel beyond automated tests.



The image below is a real character-selection screenshot from 0.9.1; this selection screen is also in 0.9.2.

comments.author: super-dev-fun
comments.body:
I’m early on working on my game so I just try to playtest plus feedback to check game feel.  

I’m a sucker for these games so played through the first full mission/level.  I had no issues and this is pretty fun.  Keep up the great work!

replies.author: DuckQuack8
replies.body: thank you feedback like this really helps while I use the AI a lot of the ideas and how it was written was mine It just helped me put it together and learn the parts of the code I didn't understand
